Package io.webagent4j.workflow

Record Class WorkflowValidationReport

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.webagent4j.workflow.WorkflowValidationReport
Record Components:
workflowId - the validated definition's identifier
diagnostics - every diagnostic found, in definition-traversal order - empty if valid()
diagnosticsTruncated - whether more diagnostics existed than this report's bounded capacity could hold - see docs/workflow.md#validation-report
requiredInputs - every declared required input, in declaration order - name, type, and secret classification only, never a value
optionalInputs - every declared optional input, in declaration order
outputs - every structurally valid declared output found, in definition-traversal order
stepCount - the number of steps successfully analyzed (a step whose own ID collided with an earlier one is not counted, since its contents were never analyzed)
conditionalCount - the number of WorkflowStepType.CONDITIONAL steps analyzed
maximumObservedConditionalDepth - the deepest conditional nesting level actually reached during analysis - may exceed Workflow.MAX_CONDITIONAL_NESTING_DEPTH by exactly one for an invalid, over-deep definition, never more, since analysis never recurses past the step that first exceeds the limit
public record WorkflowValidationReport(WorkflowId workflowId, List<WorkflowValidationDiagnostic> diagnostics, boolean diagnosticsTruncated, List<WorkflowVariable<?>> requiredInputs, List<WorkflowVariable<?>> optionalInputs, List<WorkflowValidationOutput> outputs, int stepCount, int conditionalCount, int maximumObservedConditionalDepth) extends Record
Immutable, deterministic, backend-neutral explanation of a Workflow definition's static properties, produced without ever executing anything - see Workflow.Builder.validate() and docs/workflow.md#validation-report.

This is a structural sibling to WorkflowExecutionPlan, not the same concept: the report explains whether and why a definition is valid; the plan explains what a valid definition can structurally execute. Neither depends on an actual execution existing, unlike WorkflowExecutionTree, which exists only after one.

Workflow.Builder.validate() and Workflow.Builder.build() derive their conclusions from the exact same internal analysis - never two independently maintained rule sets that could diverge. build() remains fail-closed: it rejects an invalid definition exactly as before, whether or not a caller ever calls validate() first, and this report never makes an invalid definition executable.
